The second man's hand stays under the table. Just in case.

Fast. Good instinct.

Your hand clamps his wrist before he can decide. You haul it up into the lamplight.

Empty. No steel. Just a hand, rigid with surprise, the fingers splayed.

A beat of silence.

The big one doesn't move. Doesn't reach. He watches you with something that might be respect, or might be the careful stillness of a man who doesn't want to escalate in a room this small.

"Easy," he says. Quietly.

The second man, younger up close, jaw tight, lets out a slow breath through his nose. You haven't let go.

"He keeps it there out of habit," the big one says. "Bad knee. Steadies himself." A pause. "We came to talk. If Maren wanted you dead she'd have let the Saltmen sort it."

You hold the wrist another moment. Let the point land. Then release.

The younger one pulls his hand back. Doesn't rub the wrist. Pride, what's left of it.

"Midday tomorrow," the big one repeats. "Come alone." He stands, unhurried, buttons his coat against the cold he's about to walk into. "She's not your enemy, Vail. Not yet."

They leave through the front door. The ferryman's track east swallows them inside a minute.

Calder Ashvane wipes the bar. Says nothing. The ale in your cup has gone cold.
